headline: Messi laughs as security finds BBQ tools in teammate's bag at airport
summary: Lionel Messi and the Argentina squad were caught in a funny moment at Miami airport after security discovered unusual items in Cristian Romero's luggage.
details: Lionel Messi and his teammates faced strict security screenings at Miami airport, including metal detectors, while traveling for their upcoming match against Cape Verde.
The serious atmosphere turned into laughter when security officers discovered a large barbecue lighter and oversized barbecue tongs in the suitcase of defender Cristian Romero.
The security personnel were visibly surprised by the discovery of the cooking tools, which led to the entire Argentina squad, including Messi, bursting into laughter.
It was revealed that Romero had packed the equipment specifically to prepare traditional Argentine asado (barbecue) during the tournament.
The incident has since gone viral, showing a lighter side of the world's best player and his teammates during their high-pressure travel schedule.
caption:
Imagine being the world's greatest footballer and bursting into laughter because your teammate packed BBQ tongs in his suitcase!

The security personnel were visibly surprised by the discovery of the cooking tools, which led to the entire Argentina squad, including Messi, bursting into laughter.

It was revealed that Romero had packed the equipment specifically to prepare traditional Argentine asado (barbecue) during the tournament.

The incident has since gone viral, showing a lighter side of the world's best player and his teammates during their high-pressure travel schedule.

headline_marked: 28 killed: [[Landslides plague Rohingya camps]] in Cox's Bazar
headline: 28 killed: Landslides plague Rohingya camps in Cox's Bazar
summary: Between 2021 and 2026, landslides have claimed 28 lives and injured 80 in the refugee settlements, with 2024 being the deadliest year.
details: Landslides in the Rohingya camps of Cox's Bazar killed 28 people and injured at least 80 between 2021 and 2026, according to the UNHCR. The deadliest year was 2024, when 12 people lost their lives.

The risk is driven by a combination of steep terrain, deforestation from the 2017 emergency settlements, and extreme population density. Many families are forced to build homes on unstable slopes, making them prone to sudden collapse during heavy rain.

A global humanitarian funding crisis has forced agencies to scale back critical risk-reduction activities. This includes a reduction in the maintenance of drainage systems and the slope stabilisation work needed to prevent disasters.
Relocating families from high-risk areas remains a major challenge. The camps are among the most densely populated places in the world, with almost no vacant land available for safer alternatives.

Many refugees are reluctant to move because they fear losing access to their social networks, markets, and livelihoods. As a result, thousands continue to live in fear every monsoon, using temporary measures like sandbags and bamboo poles to protect their shelters.
caption:
28 dead and 80 injured. For thousands of Rohingya refugees, the monsoon is no longer a season—it's a recurring test of survival.

Landslides in the Rohingya camps of Cox's Bazar killed 28 people and injured at least 80 between 2021 and 2026, according to the UNHCR. The deadliest year was 2024, when 12 people lost their lives.

The risk is driven by a combination of steep terrain, deforestation from the 2017 emergency settlements, and extreme population density. Many families are forced to build homes on unstable slopes, making them prone to sudden collapse during heavy rain.

A global humanitarian funding crisis has forced agencies to scale back critical risk-reduction activities. This includes a reduction in the maintenance of drainage systems and the slope stabilisation work needed to prevent disasters.

Relocating families from high-risk areas remains a major challenge. The camps are among the most densely populated places in the world, with almost no vacant land available for safer alternatives.

Many refugees are reluctant to move because they fear losing access to their social networks, markets, and livelihoods. As a result, thousands continue to live in fear every monsoon, using temporary measures like sandbags and bamboo poles to protect their shelters.
